about.text: Cheese whose curd is cut to the size of wheat grains, heated to around 50 °C and pressed, then ripened for three months to over three years, until it holds no more than 56 % water in the cheese without its fat. Emmentaler, Parmesan, Grana Padano and Pecorino are among them.

Sardinia's PDO sheep cheese, one of Italy's major pecorini and made in large volumes.
The Basque Country's smoked PDO sheep cheese, a defining cheese of northern Spain.

Sardinia's ancient PDO sheep cheese, shepherd-made for millennia and the island's traditional smoked wheel.
